introduction.p: Lines and circles are not the only curves that appear in calculus. Parabolas are the basic graphs of quadratic functions. Ellipses appear in planetary motion and optimization. Hyperbolas appear in reciprocal functions, asymptotes, and polar coordinates.
These curves are called conic sections, or simply conics, because they can be obtained by slicing a cone with a plane. For our purposes, the most important skill is algebraic recognition.

p.em: Which squared terms appear? What are their signs? Can we complete the square?

subsection.title: Recognizing conics quickly
subsection.p: When no xy-term appears, the squared terms give a quick first test for a nondegenerate conic. Complete the square and check the constants: degenerate equations can instead describe a point, one or two lines, or the empty set.
A circle is the special ellipse in which the two squared terms have the same coefficient after completing the square.
